summary: The core is broken into modules that match board blocks: sync chain, position control, motion-object vertical/horizontal control, picture-ROM shift registers, the line-buffer pair, color RAM and the 74LS259 output latches. Every module is written as counters, latches, adders and gate equations clocked from the H/V raster counters. MAME draws all sprites once per frame through gfx transpen and computes scroll offsets in arithmetic. The core instead does per-scanline vertical matching, uses shift-register pixel output and ping-pong line buffers, and drives scroll from hardware counters. The only clear MAME-shaped detail is the 0x18 clamp on the vertical scroll address.

findings.signal: sprite engine is a scan-time line-buffer pipeline
findings.note: Sprites are found by adding VC to SR[15:8] and checking that the top nibble is 1111 (MATCHn). Two loadable/clearable 8-bit address counters feed ping-pong 4-bit buffer RAMs (ic10A/ic10B), which swap on DIP2. MAME instead loops over the sprite list once per frame into a sprite bitmap.

findings.signal: 74194-style shift registers for sprite pixels, with flip done by shift direction
findings.note: The ROM nibbles go into three 4-bit universal shift registers (ic9D/9B/9C). Their S0/S1 mode is driven by SHFT0/SHFT1, and the output bit is the MSB or the LSB depending on PLAYER2. That is how a board flips pixels, unlike MAME's flipx/flipy arguments.

findings.signal: position control decoded from H/V counter bits
findings.note: LD1n/LD2n, CL1n/CL2n, SHFT0/1, CK1 and DIP2 are gate equations on HC[2:0] and VC[0] (ic9F/9H/9J/10H/10J). The sprite fetch and load phases therefore come from the raster counter, as on the board. Nothing in MAME has this structure.

findings.signal: sync and IRQ from counter-bit equations, not a PROM table scan
findings.note: The H/V counters are given chip labels (7N/7M/7P...). VBLANK and VSYNC are sum-of-products of vcount bits, and IRQCLK is ~vcount[5], which drives an edge-triggered flip-flop (ic11R) cleared by INTACKn. MAME scans the sync PROM to find edges and sets timers.

findings.signal: scroll done with loadable raster counters
findings.note: The horizontal scroll register counts up or down at the pixel clock during active video. The vertical one is reloaded from vr during VBLANK and steps on each HSYNC edge, up or down depending on PLAYER2. MAME computes (m_hscroll + (x ^ flip)) per pixel instead.

findings.signal: vertical address clamp matches MAME's guess
findings.mame_ref: src/mame/atari/ccastles.cpp:screen_update ('if (effy < 24) effy = 24', marked as a guess about POTATO)
findings.note: The line `vs = vi <= 8'h18 ? 8'h18 : vi` repeats MAME's guessed clamp on the effective Y address rather than a mechanism derived from the board. It is small, but it is the one carry-over of a MAME expression.

findings.signal: priority PROM written as gate equations on MV/MPI/BIT3
findings.note: The select and color-bit-4 outputs are written as sum-of-products over MV[2:0], MPI and BIT[3], and feed the address mux of the 82S09 color RAM (ic10R). MAME builds a PROM index and does a table lookup.

findings.signal: bit-mode read-modify-write timed to bus phases
findings.note: The DRAM is shared between video (hs/vs) and CPU (DRBA) on alternate ce5 phases. Bit-mode writes merge the new nibble with data latched at ce2Hd2 and write at ce2Hd3. The X/Y autoincrement counters work as hardware up/down counters. This does not follow MAME's wpprom lookup or its nibble replication, though the write-protect is reduced to DRBA[14:12]!=0, which is a simplification.

findings.signal: address decode as a gate tree with chip-labelled intermediate nets
findings.note: Chip selects come out of cascaded decoder terms (w5R_6R, w6R_6L6M5M feeding ic6M outputs), and the write strobes are gated by ~BRWn & ce2Hd. MAME uses an address_map of handlers. The memory map itself is neutral; the structure is the board's.
This is a 4-bit counter (ic8M) that counts VBLANK rising edges, is cleared by WDOGn, and asserts reset from bit 3. That is the board's counter, not MAME's generic watchdog_timer_device.
MAME models the same two LS259 addressable latches, and both sides compute STORE = ~q2 & q3. A correct core and a correct emulator must share this, so it counts neither way.
